Research

Opto-mechanical levitating sensors

Optically and magnetically levitated mesoscopic sensors as a route to ultra-low-threshold detection — sensitivity projections, signal modelling and physics-case studies for a new class of experiment.

Overview

Optically and magnetically levitated mesoscopic particles are among the most sensitive force and acceleration sensors ever built. By isolating a nanoscale or microscale object from its environment and reading out its motion with quantum-limited precision, levitated opto-mechanical systems can probe forces far too small for conventional detectors.

The group studies how this emerging technology could extend dark matter searches into mass regimes — and interaction types — inaccessible to conventional direct-detection experiments.

Current activities

Current work focuses on sensitivity projections, signal modelling, and the physics-case studies that motivate this new class of experiment, alongside sensor development.
